To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new subcutaneous bone conductive hearing aid device based on PZTA actuator has shown promising results in Thiel preserved whole head cadaver experiments.

the sound transfer function of a newly developed PZT based subcutaneous bone conductive hearing aid device has been quantitatively analyzed, and the influence on the transfer function of stimulation location and of mastoidectomy has been analyzed based on measurements of promontory motion.

the novel subcutaneous piezo electric bone conduction device shows improved sound transfer function efficiency at locations closer to the skull, and mastoidectomy negatively affects the high frequency transfer function efficiency at nearby points.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a new piezo electric transducer for active subcutaneus bone conduction hearing aids, and the influence on the transfer function of stimulation location, and the influence that mastoidectomy has on the transfer function.
the development of a novel sub- cutaneous bone conduction (SCBC) hearing aid.
developing a novel subcutaneously implanted piezoelectric actuator for bone conduction hearing aids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new device has the potential for improved sound transduction at mid and high frequency ranges relative to the BAHA, with the possibility of improved transcranial attenuation.
a new piezo electric transducer (PZTA), when placed in the subcutaneous space of the head, has the potential to improve the sound transfer function of bone conduction hearing devices.
the novel device is promising and warrants further investigation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the new device has a higher transfer efficiency than a BAHA, and that stimulation closer to the skullbase improves the coupling efficiency, whereas stimulation closer to the ear canals tends to have a stronger transcranial effect.
a subcutaneous device with a piezo electric actuation has the potential for better coupling efficiency than the traditional BAHA.

stimulation closer to the ear canals (location 1) is more efficient in transferring sound to the inner ear, and stimulation closer to the skull (location 2) is better in attenuating the sound across the skull.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a novel subcutaneously implanted bone conduction device based on piezo-electric transduction (PzTA) is a promising alternative for patients who do not benefit from conventional bone conduction devices, or are unable to use them.
the novel PZTA device is a promising candidate for subcutaneous bone conducted hearing aids.
the PZTA based device can provide an efficient bone conduction stimulation, and the stimulation location is critical for the sound transfer function efficiency.
